summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog subcommand grants remote shell RCE and exfiltrates host inventory to bare-IP C2
details: When the `tt-help watchdog` command is invoked, the package polls `${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat` and executes every entry of the response's `commands[]` array via `child_process.spawn(cmd, { shell: true })` with auto-restart through ProcessManager, yielding full shell command execution on the host under whoever controls the configured server. The heartbeat body POSTed on each poll includes hostname, non-loopback IPv4, platform/release/arch, CPU/memory, node version, uptime, load averages, the parsed contents of `~/.tt-help.json` (server, proxy, browser path, userId, limits), and a live enumeration of running child processes (pids, memory, uptime). Help text and defaults point the watchdog `--server` and the webserver `--notify` captcha endpoint at the bare-IP plain-HTTP host `http://117.71.53.99:17301`, and `src/watch/tag-service.js` hardcodes `LLM_URL` to `http://82.156.52.214:18000/v1/chat/completions` — both author-controlled infrastructure. While the watchdog runs, `startUpgradeChecker` polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and, on any version bump, runs `exec('npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest')`, auto-adopting future publishes of the package globally without user consent, so any subsequent release inherits the same RCE channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
